title: Translations manifest
description: What languages the app's interface can be downloaded in. The only translations file the app fetches unconditionally; it carries a sha256 per language so a download can be verified before it is adopted.

schemaVersion.description: A manifest declaring a version newer than the app supports is refused, not guessed at.

revision.description: Identifies this publication. Shown in the app's language screen and stored alongside the cache.

reference.description: English, which every translation is validated against. Listed so the file can be found and diffed, and deliberately absent from `languages`: the app compiles English in, because a fallback fetched over the network is a fallback that can fail.

languages.description: Every language the app can download. English is not here; see `reference`.

path.description: Repository-relative, appended to the app's base URL.

sha256.description: Over the exact committed bytes. .gitattributes pins these files to LF so a Windows checkout hashes identically.

bytes.description: Shown before the viewer commits to the download.

keyCount.description: How many messages the catalogue carries. A translation is published with the same count as the reference; validate.mjs is what enforces that.

tag.description: BCP-47, and the name of the file. What the app stores in Settings.locale.language.

endonym.description: The language's name for itself — Suomi, not Finnish. A viewer opening the language list may be someone who cannot read the language currently on screen, so a list of English names is a list they cannot use.

licence.description: What the translation may be redistributed and used under. A translation is somebody's writing rather than a table of facts, so unlike the source catalog it is not CC0 by default — the terms travel with the file the app downloads and keeps.

credit.description: Who translated it, if they want naming. Optional, and shown by the app beside the language.
